theme: Giving & receiving — あげる・くれる・もらう (which direction the gift flows)
intro: Japanese picks the verb by who the gift moves toward — perfect for souvenirs and gifts on your travels.

grammar.title: Giving & receiving: あげる・くれる・もらう

rules.label: あげる (ageru) — give outward
rules.detail: I→someone, or someone→someone else; never TO me. Giver は/が, receiver に.
examples: 友だちに おみやげを あげました → tomodachi ni omiyage o agemashita (I gave my friend a souvenir)

rules.label: くれる (kureru) — give toward me
rules.detail: Receiver is me / my in-group; 私に is usually dropped. Giver は/が, receiver に.
examples: 姉が 私に 本を くれました → ane ga watashi ni hon o kuremashita (My sister gave me a book)

rules.label: もらう (morau) — receive
rules.detail: Receiver is the topic; giver marked に or から.
examples: 田中さんに チョコを もらいました → Tanaka-san ni choko o moraimashita (I got chocolate from Mr. Tanaka)

grammar.bigPoint: If the gift lands on YOU or your side, it must be くれる, never あげる. もらう tells the same event from the receiver's side.

examples.jp: 友だちに おみやげを あげました。
examples.en: I gave my friend a souvenir.

examples.jp: 姉が 私に 本を くれました。
examples.romaji: Ane ga watashi ni hon o kuremashita.
examples.en: My older sister gave me a book.

examples.jp: 田中さんに チョコを もらいました。
examples.en: I got chocolate from Mr. Tanaka.

note: The trap is あげる vs くれる — both are 'give' in English, but Japanese forces you to mark direction. If the gift comes toward you or your side, use くれる (the 私に is usually dropped). もらう flips the camera onto the receiver: same event as くれる, told as 'I received' instead of 'they gave.' Handy travel line: これ、おみやげです。どうぞ。

selfCheck.q: Your friend gave YOU a present. Fill in the blank: 友だちが プレゼントを ______ました。(あげ or くれ?)
selfCheck.a: くれました。The present came toward you, so use くれる, not あげる. You could also flip it: 友だちに プレゼントを もらいました。(I got a present from my friend.)
